messages:
nora: FYI: clarifying the exemption flow after questions this morning. Short version: exemptions are for config-only or low-risk fixes during the freeze. Model artifact changes still require a canary unless pre-approved.

deploy-bot: Exemption endpoint: `/deploy-exempt --service <svc> --env prod --reason "<short>" --owner @<you>` (audit token applied). Response SLA: 20m.

cesar (eng): Quick ask 20m SLA3 is that wall-clock or business minutes?

nora: Wall-clock. We'll try to be faster but SRE+RM have a 20m window to review.

hana (sre): Note: exemptions that touch routing or rate limits will require a short smoke canary (5m) even if no artifact change. We'll mark those in the review.

mike (release-manager): Also adding a new tag `exp-low-risk` for fast approvals. If you add that tag in the CLI it will route to the fast lane; still audited.

ivy (product): For scheduled partner pushes, can the PM request a pre-approved exemption list for known safe config keys?

nora: Yes  we can add keys to a whitelist per service. Send a PR against the handbook whitelist and tag me.

cesar (eng): ack. Will use `exp-low-risk` for small config toggles. Thanks for clarifying.

hana (sre): We'll publish a tiny FAQ in the handbook with examples (routing flag, TTL tweak, feature-flag flip). ETA EOD.

mike (release-manager): Reminding teams: canary remains mandatory for any model file swaps or quantization changes. Use staging canaries and attach eval snapshots.

nora: Thanks everyone. I'll include a 1-line note in today's release broadcast: "Exemption flow clarified: config-only fast lane, smoke canaries for routing changes, model artifacts still require canary." :white_check_mark:
file_description: clarification thread on exemption flow and canary requirements during release freezes for the release train
